newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gorbachev says ailing Yeltsin should resign.
newsitem.headline: Gorbachev says ailing Yeltsin should resign.

text.p: Mikhail Gorbachev, the last president of the Soviet Union, called on Russian leader Boris Yeltsin to resign in a radio interview on Wednesday.

"The way things are going, the president (Yeltsin) must resign," Gorbachev told Ekho Moskvy radio station. "Boris Yeltsin's (current) illness is not the first time. Over the last year the president has not worked for many months."
Gorbachev was the architect of the "perestroika" and "glasnost" reforms from 1985 until 1991 when the Soviet Union collapsed. He and Yeltsin are old sparring partners.
Gorbachev said Russia could not be "left a hostage of unclear, troubled times".

Recalling the Soviet Union's period of so-called "stagnation" under ailing Communist Party apparatchiks in the 1970s and early 1980s, Gorbachev said former Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev's long period of illness had "stopped all work...At least 10 years were lost".
Gorbachev was one of several candidates who ran against Yeltsin in the first round of Russia's presidential election this year but he won few votes.
